sections.title: What a peptide is (and is not)

items.q: How does Doctor Mike separate peptides from proteins, and what is his gold-standard example?
items.a: Both are amino-acid chains; **size is a tendency, not a law**. He treats peptides as **chemical messengers**. **Insulin** is the contrast case: lab + animal + human data and a full FDA review before it is a US prescription drug.

items.q: What distribution path does he say filled the gap after 2023 FDA compounding safety flags?
items.a: **Telehealth, longevity/functional clinics, med spas**, and gray-market sites labeled **research / not for human use** — often **self-injected** vials made abroad, often with **no clinician**.

items.q: Did the July 2026 PCAC vote FDA-approve BPC-157?
items.a: **No.** It advised whether substances belong on the **503A bulks list** (compound for a named patient). **Approval, safety-for-all, and legalization still require FDA rulemaking.** Clinics saying 'FDA approved / FDA says safe' are lying.

items.q: What human evidence did FDA scientists cite for the seven peptides?
items.a: BPC-157: **one UC enema abstract, n=53**, not a full paper; **no RCTs** for injectable tendon/muscle use. KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c: **no adequate published human exposure**. Staff recommended **no on all seven** (identity, dose, benefit, harm unknown).
**Six yes** — BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, Epitalon, Semax. **Emideltide (DSIP) no.** BPC/KPV/TB-500 reported **8–6–1**.

items.q: What winning argument does he grant is logical but off-mission?
items.a: **Harm reduction:** people will inject anyway; a licensed pharmacy beats mystery powder (including an **MDMA-laced research vial** story). Logical, but **not** the usefulness / safety / manufacturing question the process is built to answer.

items.q: What incentive does he say a demand-first 503A path creates?
items.a: Skip trials. **Influencers and clinics create demand**, then treat that demand as proof that access is necessary — **profit from demand instead of proof**. He calls it a **worse pharma**: no proof required, COI-friendly.
